notes: No school- or computing-unit AI policy found at Michigan Tech (searched: none-found); course layer deferred, so this file characterizes the university layer only. Reconciled from two independent codings. Exact repeats of the shared sentences across the three syllabus templates are coded once (first occurrence). The Dean of Students integrity page has one AI sentence; its contract-cheating text does not mention AI and is not coded. Unit stance is neutral for disclosure, citation, accountability and definition units, and non-neutral only where the unit itself prohibits, restricts, permits or encourages AI use. One unit (cite authorized resources, HU 3015) was added by the reconciler.

units.policy: Instructors should make sure to clarify to students what is acceptable and unacceptable use of GAI tools and systems in their syllabus and assignments.

units.policy: Faculty should not opt out of understanding AI; it is important to become familiar with AI tools that might be employed by students to complete work in the course.

units.frag_start: faculty can and should identify uses
units.policy: Faculty can and should identify uses of AI compatible with their course goals and identify ways to integrate it into their courses to prepare students for AI use in their future area of work.

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P35 (redesign assignments), coder B P63 (support faculty in learning AI). The passage suggests running one's own assignment prompt through GAI to see what it produces; it is advice to learn what AI does, not a redesign of assignments, so P63.

units.policy: Faculty should build in opportunities within their academic unit to share their approach to classroom use of AI (policy statement, pedagogical uses, guidance to students), particularly for courses that are sequential or prerequisites.

documents.title: About Michigan Tech's Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The Dean of Students' academic integrity page defines misconduct and, under cheating, adds one sentence making GAI use that the instructor prohibits or that does not follow University Policy 1.20 an integrity violation. The rest of the page concerns misconduct generally.
documents.stance_why: The only AI statement is that GAI use 'in ways that are prohibited by the instructor or that do not comport with University Policy 1.20' is a violation, which makes the instructor the one who sets the rule, so the document delegates.

units.why: The sentence classes prohibited or non-compliant GAI use as an integrity violation, P36; it also makes the instructor's prohibition the standard (P04), but the misconduct classification is the main content.
units.anchor: will also be regarded as an academic integrity violation
units.frag_start: Use of generative artificial intelligence technologies
units.policy: Use of generative artificial intelligence technologies (GAI) in ways that are prohibited by the instructor or that do not comport with University Policy 1.20 will also be regarded as an academic integrity violation.
units.resolution_why: Coder B split this sentence into three units (B00 'will also be regarded as an academic integrity violation', B01 'prohibited by the instructor', B02 'do not comport with University Policy 1.20'). The sentence states one rule, so it is one unit; codes agree between A00 and B00. B03 (a revision-history note) is not a policy and is dropped.
